It was represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] from 1987 to 2022.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} The district stretched along the [[Moro Gulf]] coast of western Maguindanao and includes [[Cotabato City]], an independent port city. [[Barira]], [[Buldon]], [[Datu Blah T. Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte|Datu Blah T. Sinsuat]], [[Datu Odin Sinsuat]], [[Kabuntalan]], [[Matanog]], [[Northern Kabuntalan]], [[Parang, Maguindanao del Norte|Parang]], [[Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte|Sultan Kudarat]], [[Sultan Mastura]] and [[Upi, Maguindanao del Norte|Upi]] are the district's constituent municipalities.{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} From 2006 to 2008, the district was briefly replaced by the lone district of [[Shariff Kabunsuan]], a short-lived province that was carved out of the same area in Maguindanao and which was eventually nullified by the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]]. It was last represented in the [[19th Congress of the Philippines|19th Congress]] by Sittie Shahara Mastura of [[Lakas-CMD]], who was later redistricted to [[Maguindanao del Norte's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the newly established province of [[Maguindanao del Norte]] in 2022.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan="2" | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan="2" | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
